sentences.text:
Case :- Writ - C No. - 34575 of 2022
Petitioner :- Kalawati @ Kamlawati

Respondent :- Union Of India And 3 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Rajesh Kumar Dubey,Sachin Kumar Upadhyay

Counsel for Respondent :- A.S.G.I.,Anil Kumar Rai,C.S.C.,Pranjal Mehrotra
Hon'ble Mahesh Chandra Tripathi,J.
Hon'ble Vivek Kumar Singh,J.
Heard Sri Rajesh Kumar Dubey, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri Amrish Shukla, learned
Additional Chief Standing Counsel for the State-respondents and Sri Pranjal Mehrotra, learned
counsel who appears for the fifth respondent i.e. National Highway Authority of India through its
Project Director, District Ghazipur.
This writ petition has been preferred under Article 226 of the Constitution of India with a request to
quash the notification dated 30.11.2015 with regard to the petitioners Land Khasara No. 270 Kha
area 0.0190 hectare (only 30 Feet on the South Side and 10 Feet in the North Side) and further for
direction in the nature of mandamus commanding the respondents to pay the compensation for the
remaining land of the petitioner acquired by the authorities as per commercial rate as prescribed
under law.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Sri Pranjal Mehrotra, learned counsel for the fifth respondent has raised two fold preliminary objections regarding maintainability of the writ petition, firstly the acquisition proceedings took place in the year 2015 and admittedly the award was also made on 25.03.2017 but the said acquisition proceedings is not under challenge and as such on the ground of delay and latches, the writ petition is liable to be dismissed at the admission stage itself.
Secondly, the relief for enhancement of compensation, the petitioner has got an efficacious remedy to approach the Arbitrator under the National Highways Act, 1956.
He has placed reliance upon the Section 3G (5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 and in the present matter, the Arbitrator is concerned Collector.

The said provision provides that if the amount determined by the competent authority under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) is not acceptable to either of the parties, the amount shall, on an application by either of the parties, be determined by the Arbitrator to be appointed by the Central Government and as such, the present writ petition is liable to be dismissed on the ground of availability of statutory remedy provided under the Section 3G (5) of the National Highways Act,
1956.

Confronted with this situation, learned counsel for the petitioner fairly states that he is not pressing the first relief and states that leave may be accorded in the light of Section 3 G (5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 so that he may press the second relief before the Arbitrator.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and without adverting to the merit of the case

,
we leave it open to the petitioner to move appropriate application in the light of provisions contained Section 3 G (5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 before the Arbitrator within two weeks from today, this Court hope and trust that the same may be considered and decided expeditiously strictly in accordance with law.
With the aforesaid observation and direction, the instant writ petition stands disposed off.

Order Date :- 16.1.2023 Jaswant  Kalawati @ Kamlawati vs Union Of India And 3 Others on 16 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162916837/
